items.stem: Which Route 53 routing policy sends users to the AWS region that gives them the lowest latency?

options.rationale: Correct: latency-based routing directs users to the lowest-latency region.
Simple routing returns one record set without latency awareness.
Weighted routing splits by weight, not by latency.
ALIAS is a record type, not a latency policy.

items.stem: Which TWO improve a global web app's delivery with CloudFront? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Cache static assets at edge locations with appropriate TTLs
options.rationale: Correct: edge caching reduces latency and origin load.

options.text: Serve HTTPS using an ACM certificate
options.rationale: Correct: TLS at the edge secures delivery for users.

options.text: Make the S3 origin publicly readable to everyone
options.rationale: A public origin bypasses CloudFront protection and is a risk.

options.text: Set a 1-second TTL on all static files to force constant refetch
options.rationale: Tiny TTLs defeat caching and raise origin load.

items.explanation: Correct: Cache static assets at edge locations with appropriate TTLs, Serve HTTPS using an ACM certificate.

items.stem: After updating a file at the origin, why might CloudFront still serve the old version?

options.text: The object is still cached at the edge until its TTL expires or it is invalidated
options.rationale: Correct: cached objects persist until TTL expiry or an invalidation.
A deleted record would stop resolution, not serve a stale file.
CloudFront caches by design; that is the point.
Certificates secure transport, not cache freshness.

items.explanation: Correct: The object is still cached at the edge until its TTL expires or it is invalidated.
